voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`). captionY (px or "high") lifts the caption above low action.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Astika sub-parva, adhyayas 33–35: Vasuki, hearing his mother's curse, calls his brothers to council: how can the curse be escaped? Some serpents say: let us become brahmins and beg Janamejaya not to hold the sacrifice; some, let us become his ministers and counsel against it; some, let us bite the chief priest; some, let us become clouds and pour rain on the fire; some, let us steal the sacrificial ladles by night. Vasuki rejects these. Then Elapatra speaks (1.34): when their mother cursed them he was in her lap and heard the gods ask Brahma how he could allow it; Brahma answered that only the wicked serpents would perish, and that the sage Jaratkaru would marry a woman of the same name, and their son Astika would free the virtuous serpents. The serpents rejoice (1.35); Vasuki, who has a sister named Jaratkaru, sets serpents to watch the sage.
structure: From episode 21: COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words, ≤ 3 s; opening chosen by content (not a fixed rotation): a question over the council in the dark, the card at the top over the vault) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band over its first shot → turn at 40–60 % after one ≈ 0.9 s rest → the cliffhanger image + line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band over the cliffhanger image that dissolves into frame 1. strings.recapLine: Shesha left to hold the earth. Vasuki stayed.

lines.text: How do you escape your own mother's curse?
lines.say: How do you escape [p:40] your own mother's curse?
lines.note: COLD OPEN (question card over the answer's place, moving from frame 1): looking down into Vasuki's hall from the vault: a ring of serpents' heads around a jewel-fire, the camera sinking toward them; the card at the top.

lines.text: Vasuki called his brothers to council.
lines.say: Vasuki [p:60] called his brothers to council.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top): NEW LIGHT, the hall lit by a central jewel-fire (ember-red under violet): Vasuki large in the centre, plaque "Vasuki".

lines.speaker: nagas
lines.text: "Let us become brahmins, and beg the king to stop."
lines.say: Let us become brahmins, [p:80] and beg the king to stop.
lines.note: STORY 1 (one serpent speaks): a VISION PANEL opens in the jewel-fire's smoke: serpents in brahmins' white, bowing before a throne.

lines.speaker: nagas
lines.say: Let us bite [p:60] the chief priest.
lines.note: STORY 2 (another): the panel turns: a serpent strikes at a priest's silhouette (stylised).

lines.speaker: nagas
lines.text: "Let us be clouds, and rain on the fire."
lines.say: Let us be clouds, [p:80] and rain on the fire.
lines.note: STORY 3 (another): the panel turns: dark clouds with serpent tails pour rain on the sacrificial fire.

lines.speaker: vasuki
lines.text: "No. Each plan is a crime, or a dream."
lines.say: No. [p:250] Each plan is a crime, [p:80] or a dream.
lines.note: STORY 4 (Vasuki speaks): close and low on Vasuki's hood (a single hood: no hand), the visions blown out of the smoke.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the youngest voice in the hall spoke.
lines.say: Then the youngest voice [p:60] in the hall spoke.
lines.note: FRAME (Sauti, a twenty-first angle: a high three-quarter view from behind the fire, Sauti's face lit, the sages as a dark ring below).

lines.speaker: elapatra
lines.text: "I heard Brahma speak of this, from our mother's lap."
lines.say: I heard Brahma speak of this, [p:100] from our mother's lap.
lines.note: STORY 5 · THE TURN (≈ 45 %): after the 0.9 s silence, Elapatra, a slender silver-teal serpent, rises out of the crowd into the jewel-light; plaque "Elapatra".

lines.text: The gods had asked Brahma why he let the curse stand.
lines.say: The gods had asked Brahma [p:60] why he let the curse stand.
lines.note: STORY 6: NEW LIGHT, the memory in silver-blue: Brahma on his lotus in a cold moonlit court, the gods below him as small luminous figures; a serpent child in the corner.

lines.speaker: brahma
lines.text: "A sage named Jaratkaru will marry a girl of his own name."
lines.say: A sage named Jaratkaru [p:80] will marry a girl [p:40] of his own name.
lines.note: STORY 7 (Brahma speaks, in the memory): Brahma large, frontal, his lower hand raised; two small linked medallions appear: a gaunt sage, a girl with a serpent crown.

lines.speaker: brahma
lines.text: "Their son will save the good serpents."
lines.say: Their son [p:60] will save the good serpents.
lines.note: STORY 8: a third medallion between the two: a small boy, lit gold; the serpents' eyes all turn to it.

lines.text: And Vasuki had a sister. Her name was Jaratkaru.
lines.say: And Vasuki had a sister. [p:300] Her name was Jaratkaru.
lines.note: STORY 9: back in the hall at full warmth: Vasuki turns to his sister, a young naga woman with a single-hood crown, at the edge of the light; she looks up.

lines.text: So the serpents watched for Jaratkaru, a sage who never wanted a wife.
lines.say: So the serpents watched for Jaratkaru, [p:150] a sage who never wanted a wife.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (cliffhanger, the catalog line): NEW LIGHT, a forest at night in teal moonlight: serpents' eyes glint in the roots and branches; far off, a gaunt ascetic walks alone along a path.

lines.text: Next: The Ancestors in the Pit
